summary: Replay over 97 PRs with simulated approvals: loop caught 11 of 16 positives (baseline 10), noise 30 of 60 controls (baseline 33), routed 10 of 21 non-positives (baseline 12); later half (PR index 48-96): loop 6 of 9 catches, 17 of 27 noise vs baseline 5 and 20; 23 overrides accepted. Verdict: beats baseline: 11 vs 10 catches, 30 vs 33 noise.

The headline stays this pre-declared loop.

tried.change: after seeing the first run: added optional gate guards (loop.GUARDS) as two extra variants, not as the default. Why: in the first run, on 2019-06-10, before any positive had been decided, the gate accepted excluding path prefix src/MessagePack/ from wire-format ('caught must not drop' is vacuous with no positives), which later lost #2139; and general-choice reached its low noise by excluding the contracts' own declared paths (e.g. src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/ from generated). Guards: min-positives: narrow needs at least one positive among the replayed PRs (otherwise 'caught must not drop' is vacuous); declared-paths: narrow may not exclude a whole declared contract path (a path prefix equal to or above a project.json path of that contract, a directory segment derived from one, or the file name of a declared file; declared files include the files the contract's `sources` cite).
tried.result: first version of the guards (prefixes and segments only): guarded 12 vs 10 catches, 31 vs 33 noise; general-choice-guarded 12 vs 10 catches, 26 vs 33 noise

tried.change: after reviewing the live proposals list (propose.py, guards on by default there): declared-paths widened to also block excluding the file name of a declared file (it offered excluding MessagePackReader.cs and MessagePackWriter.cs from wire-format) and the files a contract's `sources` cite (it offered excluding src/MessagePack/MessagePack.csproj, the file that declares the targets, from targets).

method.stream: evidence/pr-stream.json prs sorted by (date, pr); date = history.json date (merge/close date, not the open date) or control merge date.
method.start_state: k=0: the 2025 baseline generalised contracts (pr-stream.json details.generalised_rules + project.json paths).
method.decision_availability: max(decision when, PR date); fed to the loop only before PRs dated strictly later than that day, so a PR never sees its own decision and same-day PRs never see each other's.
method.learning_step: for each day D on which decisions become available: loop.propose_contracts(cutoff=D) over all available decisions, each proposal gated (loop.gate) on the PRs available on or before D; every eligible proposal accepted in order (widen first, then narrow, stream order of trigger), re-gated on the state after the earlier acceptances.
method.routed: a promise contract (public-api, wire-format, generated, targets, diagnostics, security) trips; user-docs is not a promise.
method.caught: positive (concern in backtest.POSITIVE_CONCERNS) with a tripped contract in its expected_contracts.
method.non_positives: history PRs whose concern is not a promise (maintainability, performance, scope, ...): not scored as catches or noise; how many are routed is reported separately.
method.not_used: rule_ids_cited (rules mined from these same PRs: leakage); rule proposals; --llm.
method.attribution: accepted_overrides[].later_*: for each later PR, the outcome with the state active at that PR vs the same state without that override.

limits: Small stream: 16 positives (6 missed by the baseline) and 60 controls; one PR is about 6 points of catch rate and under 2 points of noise rate.
The 2025 contracts were written after these PRs (k=0 start state); the baseline already benefits from hindsight (limit listed in evidence/backtest.json).
Approval is simulated: every eligible proposal is accepted. A real owner may reject some; the replay shows what the gate alone allows.
The gate only sees PRs decided before the cutoff; a feature that passes on a few past PRs can still add noise on later ones (see accepted_overrides[].later_hurt).
Positive labels and expected contracts come from history.json concern labels (hand, from maintainer comments); a wrong label moves a PR between caught and missed.
Line-pattern candidates see only cached lines: on the PRs marked truncated in pr-stream.json, lines beyond the cap are kept only if they match a baseline pattern.
Controls carry no recorded pushback but history.json came from targeted searches; some controls may have had review pushback we could not see, so noise is an upper bound.
date is the merge/close date, so a PR can be predicted after discussions that, in reality, happened earlier; the open date is not in the cache.
